intent: Provide a URL shortener service that creates short links from long URLs, redirects short codes to their original URLs, returns link details, and exposes per-link click analytics (total clicks and last click time) through an API.

functional_needs.statement: A client can create a short link by submitting a long URL; the system returns a short code for that link.
functional_needs.source_quote: Create a short link from a long URL

functional_needs.statement: Requesting a short code redirects the caller to the original long URL.
functional_needs.source_quote: redirect from the short code to the original URL

functional_needs.statement: A client can retrieve the details of an existing short link.
The system records the total number of clicks (redirects) for each short link.
functional_needs.source_quote: Total click count per short link

functional_needs.statement: The system records the timestamp of the most recent click for each short link.
functional_needs.source_quote: plus the timestamp of the last click

functional_needs.statement: A client can retrieve a short link's analytics (total click count and last click timestamp) through an API call for that link.
functional_needs.source_quote: exposed via an API call for that link

nfr_asks.text: Generic 'reliability features'; per clarification C-1 the user selected no catalog entry, so no NFR is added.

ambiguities.question: Which HTTP redirect status should the redirect use: temporary (302/307) or permanent (301/308)?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: The status code is externally visible, and permanent redirects are cached by browsers, so repeat visits would bypass the service and not be counted as clicks.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Use a temporary redirect (302) so every click reaches the service and is counted.

ambiguities.question: What counts as a click: every redirect request served, or only unique visitors?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Determines the click count value returned by the analytics API and what data must be kept.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Every successful redirect request increments the count by one.

ambiguities.question: When the same long URL is submitted more than once, should the system return the existing short link or create a new one?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Changes the create response and how click counts are split across links.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Create a new short link on every request.
options: Always create a new short link
Return the existing short link for the same URL

ambiguities.question: Can clients choose a custom short code (alias), or are codes always system-generated?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Affects the create request shape and conflict handling.
options: Optional custom alias with conflict error

ambiguities.question: Which long URLs are accepted on create?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Determines which create requests are rejected as invalid.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Accept only absolute http and https URLs; reject anything else with a validation error.

ambiguities.question: Which fields should a short link's details include?
ambiguities.recommended_default: Short code, original URL, and creation timestamp; analytics are returned by their own call.
options: Short code, original URL, creation timestamp
Same plus click count and last click timestamp

ambiguities.question: What should happen when a requested short code does not exist (redirect, details, or analytics)?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Defines error behavior visible to clients.

ambiguities.question: What should the analytics call return for the last click timestamp of a link that has never been clicked?
ambiguities.why_it_matters: Defines the analytics response for new links.
ambiguities.recommended_default: Click count 0 and last click timestamp null.

out_of_scope: Rate limiting, contract-based input validation (SEC-INPUT), and Prometheus metrics: no NFR selected per C-1
Uptime, failover, and durability guarantees (cannot be built or validated per C-1)
Analytics beyond total click count and last click timestamp (e.g., referrers, geography, devices, time-series breakdowns)
User accounts, authentication, and link ownership
